verdict: Adobe opened its year with record revenue of $6.4B, up 12%, and record operating cash flow of $3.0B, as AI-first recurring revenue more than tripled and subscriptions grew 13%.

kpis.label: Total ARR
kpis.note: annualized recurring revenue at quarter end

segments.name: Subscription
segments.note: Creative Cloud, Acrobat and Experience Cloud subscriptions — 97 cents of every revenue dollar. Creative & Marketing Professionals paid $4,390M (+12%); Business Professionals & Consumers paid $1,780M (+16%).

segments.name: Product
segments.note: One-time software licenses — a small legacy line from before Adobe moved to subscriptions.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Consulting, training and support services sold alongside the software.

flow.costPlain: Running Adobe's cloud services — data centers, customer support and the cost of delivering its software.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building Photoshop, Acrobat, Firefly AI and the rest of the product line.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Sales teams, advertising and marketing — Adobe's biggest running cost.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day: finance, legal, HR, offices.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of technology and customer relationships bought in past acquisitions.

otherDetail: Non-operating items added $4M: $62M of other income and $5M of investment gains, less $63M of interest expense.
footerNote: Revenue is split by type, not by customer group.
pngFooterNote: Revenue is split by type, not by customer group.
follow100Note: Adobe keeps about $29.52 of every $100 — and note that sales & marketing ($26.70) still costs it more per $100 than research & development ($17.35). Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: A record quarter, again
takeaways.text: Revenue hit a record $6,398M, up 12% (11% in constant currency), and GAAP net income rose to $1,889M. Remaining performance obligations — work customers have already committed to — stood at $22.22B.

takeaways.title: AI products are scaling
takeaways.text: AI-first annualized recurring revenue more than tripled year over year, and total ARR reached $26.06B. Business Professionals & Consumers subscription revenue grew 16% to $1.78B, faster than the creative professional line's 12%.

takeaways.title: Cash flow set a Q1 record
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was a first-quarter record $2.96B — more than the quarter's $1.89B of net income, because customers pay for subscriptions up front.
